newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 17.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
K.R. NARAYANAN SET TO BE NEXT PRESIDENT

The Congress party and the ruling United Front coalition on Monday decided to nominate Vice President K.R. Narayanan as their presidential candidate. The decision was taken in a one-to-one meeting between Congress party president Sitaram Kesri and the United Front convenor. The vice president will be a joint candidate of the Congress and the United Front. This is the first time a presidential candidate is being jointly nominated by two parties. Narayanan thus will have the immediate support of 69.5 percent of the electoral college.
The Economic Times
LEFT PARTIES STALL MOVE TO HIKE PETROLEUM PRICES AGAIN

The leftwing parties in the ruling coalition once again blocked the move to hike prices of petroleum products despite Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's statement about the urgent need to raise their prices. The parties latched on to technicalities, deferring a decision till June 27. Considering the stiff attitude of the Left, it is doubtful whether the government will get the approval of the steering committee of the ruling United Front even at its next meeting to raise the prices. Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy said there was a difference of opinion within the alliance and solving it would take time.
INDIA GATEWAY FUND WINDS UP OPERATIONS IN A DAY

The medium-sized offshore India Gateway Fund has disposed of its entire portfolio of $21 million in the market and wound up its operations. The fund was due for redemptions on June 30. It held stocks in medium- and small-cap Indian companies. These shares were sold on behalf of the fund by Peregrine Securities Limited, an associate of the Hong Kong-based investor. This is the first time in recent years an offshore fund has closed its operations by disposing of its entire stocks in a single day.
DIVESTMENT MAY BE CONFINED TO ONLY GAIL, IOC AND MTNL

The government divestment in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) may be confined to the GAIL, the Indian Oil Corp and India's basic telecommunications monopoly Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL). It is unlikely to be a broad-based exercise as earlier expected. Officials said the sales proceeds from the three blue-chip government companies would be sufficient to meet the 45 billion rupee target set in the budget. The divestment is intended to raise resources, and if the resource target for fiscal 1997/98 can be raised by selective divestment in a few companies, it will be better than wholesale selling at this point, said the officials.
VOLUNTARY DISCLOSURE SCHEME TO SEEK ASSETS' PRICE

The Voluntary Disclosure of Income Scheme (VDIS) 1997 does not allow for disclosure of wealth, but if the undisclosed income is in the form of assets, they will be valuated. The Central Board of Direct Taxes said if the undisclosed income was in jewellery acquired before April 1, 1987, it would be disclosed at the market value on that date. But when the undisclosed income is in the form of flats, land, machinery, shares and other assets acquired before April 1, 1987, then its value will be that as on the date of purchase. It also said in the case of immovable property, the declarants need not file a valuation certificate along with their declaration.
STATE BANK OF INDIA OFFICERS TO CONTINUE STRIKE

The fourth round of talks on Monday between officers and the management of the State Bank of India (SBI) failed. The bank's indefinite strike will continue on Tuesday all over the states of Maharashtra and Goa. The officers' association has called for a strike on June 19 at 13 local head offices that transact 75 percent of SBI's business. The Bank is also slated to announce its results for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) on June 19. If further talks fail as well, there will be a nation-wide strike on June 23.
Financial Express
NEW GUIDELINES FOR OVERSEAS CAR VENTURES COMING

The directorate general of foreign trade (DGFT) has set new guidelines for overseas car ventures. These will be submitted for government approval this week. One of the suggestions is to relax export guidelines for such projects to seven years instead of the present five. The DGFT also proposed a phased level of localisation in which 50 percent must be reached in three yeas and 70 percent in five years. Other suggestions include a minimum foreign equity participation of $50 million in all car ventures. It also lays down that a production facility must be in place within a reasonable period after receiving FIPB approval.
LARGEST GLOBAL REINSURANCE FIRM SETS EYES ON INDIA

Munich Re, the largest reinsurance company in the world, is the latest company to enter the race for India's health insurance sector. The company is expected to enter India through one of its many global subsidiaries. With the entry of Munich Re, the number of front-ranking companies vying for a health insurance licence has reached five. The other four companies are Aetna and Cigna of the United States, Ailianz of Germany and the British United Provident Association of the United Kingdom.
Business Standard
MULTINATIONALS' TRANSFER PRICING UNDER SCRUTINY

The Finance Ministry is studying the transfer pricing policy adopted by multinational companies with respect to the dealings with their international affiliates to prevent any attempt to understate their tax liability. The system of transfer pricing determines the price at which products or technology are sold between group companies. The ministry feels that with steep cuts in import tariffs since 1991, several transnational firms are sourcing their imports from foreign group companies.
BANKS, FINANCE INSTITUTIONS SEEK PERMISSION TO IMPORT GOLD

Several banks and a few financial institutions have asked the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Commerce Ministry for permission to import gold. The RBI will appoint about 10 new agencies to import gold. It is preparing guidelines for duty-free gold imports by banks other than the State Bank of India (SBI), which is already importing gold.
DEPOSITS SURGE MAY PROMPT BANKS TO CUT SHORT-TERM RATES

Banks plan to cut short term deposit rates because of a deposit growth of more than 100 billion rupees fiscal 1997/98 (April-March). At the same time, banks are rejecting companies' short-term deposits. Time deposits grew by 141.25 billion rupees but demand deposits fell by 40.45 billion rupees between April 1 and May 23. Deposits grew by only 16.09 billion rupees during the same period in the last financial year.
The Observer
PANIC IN NONBANKING FINANCE FIRMS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has sent a circular to commercial banks directing them not to clear without prior approval outstation interest warrant cheques of 100,000 rupees and above per month, until further orders. This created a panic among non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). The Association of Leasing and Finance companies is taking up the issue with the RBI informally and is likely to do it formally soon. They feel if banks do this, it will be equivalent to cheque bouncing and can lead to their prosecution.
RESERVE BANK, HINDUSTAN LEVER, PONDS INDIA REACH ACCORD

The Reserve Bank of India has reached a settlement with Hindustan Lever (HLL) and Ponds India on pricing of shares which were given on preferential allotment to their parent company, Unilever. The consent terms were filed in the Bombay High Court following an out of court settlement. The shares of HLL in the HLL-Tomco merger deal were sanctioned by the RBI at 357 rupees and for Ponds at 620 rupees.
DELHI COURT APPOINTS TWO AGENTS TO AID CRB LIQUIDATOR

The Delhi High Court on Monday appointed two agents to help the official liquidator of CRB Capital Markets in decoding computerised account books and other documents. The court authorised the liquidator to appoint as many assistants as required in consultation with the agents to meet the situation. These assistants should be qualified professionals like chartered accountants, company secretaries and computer software experts, the court said.
HINDUSTAN AERONAUTICS REPORT ON PARTNER DUE IN THREE MONTHS

Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) will submit to the government a final report on a partner to manufacture its 50-seater aircraft within three months. HAL's chairman said a sub-committee constituted to determine the aircraft's viability and find a prospective overseas partner had received positive responses from several overseas companies -- Saab, ATR, Bombardier, Antov and Casa. As part of its entry into civil aviation, HAL will sell part of its equity to the foreign partners, said the chairman. The company will sell equity only in its civil aviation business.
